source: Each college's own admissions or school-of-nursing page (sourceUrl per college); researched 2026-11-27, verify yearly

university-of-pennsylvania.note: Penn's catalog: "Our traditional four-year BSN is a direct-entry program for graduating high school seniors"; high school students apply through Penn's central undergraduate admissions office to the School of Nursing.

duke-university.note: Duke has no four-year undergraduate BSN; its only bachelor's nursing option was the 16-month accelerated ABSN, which the school says is ending in Spring 2026 and no longer admitting, pointing pre-licensure students to its Master of Nursing.

johns-hopkins-university.note: Johns Hopkins School of Nursing offers pre-licensure entry only through the MSN Entry into Nursing program (for bachelor's-degree holders); no undergraduate BSN.

columbia-university.note: Columbia Nursing dropped its bachelor's track in 2015; non-nurses enter through the 15-month Master's Direct Entry (MDE) program, which requires a prior bachelor's degree.

university-of-california-los-angeles.note: UCLA's BS (Prelicensure) is a four-year program; first-year applicants are admitted at the freshman level for fall only via the UC Application plus a School of Nursing supplemental application (statement, resume, two recommendations) due Jan 15.

emory-university.note: Students enter Emory College or Oxford College, take two years of prerequisites, and apply to the BSN in their 3rd semester; a 3.0 cumulative GPA gives guaranteed admission, below that applicants are waitlisted for committee review.

georgetown-university.note: Georgetown's BSN "is a traditional four-year direct entry undergraduate program," with the first nursing course in fall of the first year; first-years apply EA Nov 1 or RD Jan 1.

university-of-michigan-ann-arbor.note: Michigan's BSN takes first-year applicants into a full-time four-year program with clinicals from sophomore year; a separate sophomore transfer route leads to a three-year program.

university-of-virginia.note: "Prospective nursing students apply directly to the School of Nursing" for the traditional BSN (EA Nov 1, RD Jan 1); a separate 3-year transfer program also takes internal UVA applicants.

university-of-north-carolina-chapel-hill.note: Assured Admissions guarantees a BSN spot to select NC-resident first-years who keep a 3.0 cumulative and 3.0 prerequisite-science GPA (BSN starts junior fall); others apply later via intra-university transfer, for which the school "reserves ample spots."

boston-college.note: First-years interested in nursing apply directly to the Connell School of Nursing as their undergraduate division; Nursing is one of the few majors declared at application. Internal transfer into CSON is possible only after two semesters.

new-york-university.note: NYU Meyers' traditional four-year BS: 'High school graduates enter this program as first-year students in the fall,' taking liberal arts and prerequisites first and starting clinical courses junior year.

university-of-california-irvine.note: 'Our program is a direct-entry program for students admitted to the Nursing Science major as freshmen'; they do not reapply later. Admission is competitive and the program aims to graduate about 50 students a year; limited change-of-major also exists.

university-of-florida.note: Traditional BSN is limited-access upper-division entry via NursingCAS (Fall 2027 deadline Feb 1, 2027): 60 credits, 3.0 overall and 3.0 pre-professional GPA, HESI A2; 'not all qualified applicants are admitted.'

the-university-of-texas-austin.note: Freshmen select Nursing as first-choice major (fall only, Dec 1 deadline) with nursing short answers; 'The BSN degree program is direct entry, with no additional application prior to upper division course work.'

university-of-wisconsin-madison.note: Students begin as pre-nursing and apply to the Traditional BSN midway through sophomore year (min 2.75 cumulative and prerequisite GPA); admission to UW does not guarantee nursing and fewer than 50% of applicants are typically admitted.

northeastern-university.note: First-year applicants select Nursing as their major on the undergraduate application, with no separate nursing application; the pre-licensure handbook says first-year applicants are admitted directly into the Nursing program.

villanova-university.note: Undergraduate admission FAQ: 'The nursing major is a four-year, direct-admit program.' Applicants need at least one year each of high school biology and chemistry.

case-western-reserve-university.note: BSN page lists 'Direct Admission to the undergraduate program'; students apply through undergraduate admission, with no second nursing application and nursing coursework from the first semester.

the-ohio-state-university.note: Limited Direct Admission BSN seats (top 10%, ACT Math 26+, early action; must finish year one with 3.2 GPA and prerequisites at C+). Others enter Pre-Nursing and apply through the highly competitive Second-Year Enrollment Process.

rutgers-university-new-brunswick.note: Rutgers School of Nursing admits high school students each fall into the four-year traditional B.S. in nursing 'for students applying directly from high school'; New Brunswick lists School of Nursing as a first-year school choice.

university-of-rochester.note: Rochester's School of Nursing offers only accelerated bachelor's programs (12 or 24 months, for those with a prior bachelor's) and an RN-to-BS; it has no traditional four-year first-year BSN.

university-of-washington.note: The Seattle BSN is a two-year professional program after prerequisites; admission once a year (autumn, Jan 15 deadline) and 'selection is capacity constrained', with a 2.00 GPA minimum but 'usually significantly higher' in practice.

the-pennsylvania-state-university-univer.note: First-year applicants are admitted directly into the Nursing program at University Park (Dec 1 deadline, competitive); transfers and change-of-major students can't enter there. About 4,000 applicants for roughly 160 seats.

purdue-university-main-campus.note: Purdue runs a 'four-year, direct-admit baccalaureate nursing program'; it is highly competitive with limited space, and applicants should apply by the Nov 1 early action deadline.

university-of-miami.note: Freshmen accepted into the Traditional BSN are 'ensured progression into the upper division' if they finish prerequisites and keep the required GPA (handbook: 3.0 cumulative UM GPA and 2.75 prerequisite GPA at entry to junior year).

florida-state-university.note: The BSN is a limited-access upper-division major: apply after about 60 credits and prerequisites with at least a 3.0 GPA (HESI A2 required from Fall 2027). Up to 150 are admitted per cycle from 300-600 applicants; admits average a 3.7-3.8 GPA.

george-washington-university.note: GW School of Nursing lists only an Accelerated BSN (needs 60+ credits or a prior bachelor's), a Veterans BSN and an online RN-BSN; no traditional first-year four-year BSN appears on its programs or deadlines pages.

stony-brook-university-suny.note: First-year applicants are admitted to Arts and Sciences to take about 57 credits of prerequisites, then apply to the upper-division Basic Baccalaureate program (minimum 2.8 GPA); the school says it 'is not a direct admission program'.

texas-a-and-m-university.note: The Traditional BSN takes no applicants straight from high school; students finish two years of prerequisites and then apply for upper-level entry (minimums: 3.0 science and prerequisite GPA, 75% on each HESI section). Admission is competitive.

university-of-massachusetts-amherst.note: Four-year BS in Nursing admits first-years only; no transfer or change-of-major students. Highly selective (about 12% acceptance), limited by clinical placements; acceptance to UMass does not guarantee the nursing major.

university-of-minnesota-twin-cities.note: Freshmen are admitted directly into the School of Nursing (supplemental questions due Nov 1); they continue to sophomore year after completing prerequisites with a minimum 3.0 GPA both fall and spring. About 30 transfer spaces otherwise.

university-of-pittsburgh.note: High school applicants apply through Pitt admissions to the School of Nursing's first-year BSN class and must meet nursing course requirements (chemistry, biology); internal and external transfers compete for limited seats.

michigan-state-university.note: Traditional BSN is a secondary-admission program (about 120 admitted a year, 3.0 minimum GPA, 28 credits plus prerequisites). Nurse Scholar Program gives high schoolers with 3.8+ GPA a guaranteed seat if they keep a 3.4 cumulative GPA.

binghamton-university-suny.note: Decker directly admits a first-year cohort; students are nursing majors once they deposit and do not need to re-apply to the nursing program after completing prerequisites.

howard-university.note: Basic track: freshmen and sophomores complete Lower Division prerequisites, then must apply and be accepted to the Upper Division (junior/senior nursing courses) with a minimum 3.0 cumulative and 3.0 science GPA.

indiana-university-bloomington.note: Limited, competitive direct-admit seats by invitation and supplemental application; direct admits are guaranteed placement from their third semester with a 3.5 prerequisite GPA. Others start as pre-nursing and apply to the traditional BSN later.

university-of-connecticut.note: Qualified students are admitted directly to the School of Nursing as first-year students (fall only, competitive). Catalog says they may hold a 2.0 GPA until fall of second year, then must keep a 2.5 GPA to progress.

clemson-university.note: The Clemson application is also the application for a Nursing seat; freshmen admitted to Nursing do not reapply. Progression needs C or better in prerequisites and a 2.5 GPR; change-of-major seats are very limited.

drexel-university.note: Entering freshmen apply to the BSN Co-op itself, choosing a 4-year (one co-op) or 5-year (three co-ops) program through Undergraduate Admissions; no separate later application to the major is described.

university-at-buffalo-suny.note: Freshmen enter as intended nursing majors and apply to the upper-division BSN, typically spring of sophomore year (competitive; min 3.3 overall GPA). Honors College students can get guaranteed Dual Admission.

university-of-delaware.note: The four-year Traditional BSN 'welcomes students directly into the nursing program as freshmen'; nursing courses start freshman year. Change of major into nursing later is space-available only.

baylor-university.note: All entering freshmen who wish to study nursing begin in the non-degree Pre-Nursing (PNU1) major; progression needs a 2.75 cumulative and science GPA plus HESI A2 score of 80+, and School of Nursing acceptance is not guaranteed.

gonzaga-university.note: High school seniors apply to nursing through Gonzaga admission and are in the program from freshman fall; they must keep a 3.0 cumulative GPA and C grades in prerequisites. No applications from current or transfer students.

marquette-university.note: Students are admitted directly to the College of Nursing; 'acceptance as a freshman in the College of Nursing assures placement in clinical nursing courses' if they remain in good standing and follow the program plan.

texas-christian-university.note: First-year applicants apply to the nursing major (via TCU admissions plus nursing supplemental questions) as direct-admit students; to stay in the program all nursing majors must keep a TCU cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher.

rutgers-university-camden.note: High school students apply through the 'Traditional, First-Year Application' (Dec 1 deadline) straight into the Rutgers School of Nursing-Camden BSN; separate space-limited internal and external transfer tracks also exist.

university-of-illinois-chicago.note: UIC Nursing 'now accepts students directly to our program in Chicago as freshmen'. It still runs a 'very competitive' junior-level transfer admission (57 credit hours, min 2.75 GPA, fall only).

university-of-missouri.note: Freshmen are admitted as pre-nursing and apply to the clinical major, where 'admission is competitive'. Honors-eligible freshmen in the Nursing Honors Program can take direct admission with a 3.8 MU GPA.

auburn-university.note: Freshmen declare pre-nursing and apply to the upper-division BSN in the fall of sophomore year through a holistic review; 'Admission to Auburn University does not guarantee admission to the College of Nursing.'

creighton-university.note: Admitted freshmen get a seat in the College of Nursing with no later application; list Nursing on the admission application.

saint-louis-university.note: Direct-entry BSN; an older catalog lists a 3.20 GPA to stay in the nursing track. Confirm the current progression GPA.

university-of-iowa.note: From fall 2027, direct admission is the only first-year BSN route (about 168 seats); it requires an ACT/SAT score and a 3.0 GPA after year one.

st-olaf-college.note: 12-15 students are admitted directly each year; others apply competitively in the fall of sophomore year (about a 3.0 GPA).
